contract: The Python and TypeScript SDKs expose attestation_record as governed read-only state, while EAS publication and revocation remain in the dedicated service and approved signing flow.
findings: attestation_record contains governed lifecycle, evidence, reviewer, and on-chain projection fields.
Chain indexers populate attestation_record from observed on-chain records.
The dedicated EAS service submits and revokes on-chain attestations; direct row creation does neither and bypasses the governed signing workflow.
The previous SDK examples created draft database rows with placeholder or mismatched fields and described those rows as attestations.
change: Removed GenericMethods mutation inheritance and create/createMany/update/delete from both AttestationMethods surfaces. Preserved list/get/listPending/listByEntity. Updated Python and TypeScript workflow examples to read indexed attestations and documented the service boundary.
scope_limits: SDK calls were mocked; no database, provider, candidate, or legacy service was used.
This does not add a Gateway attestation-request lifecycle or replace the dedicated EAS service.
Capability classifications and MAN-CAP acceptance remain unchanged.
rollback: Restore SDK mutation methods only after an authenticated attestation-request workflow is implemented with explicit lifecycle, audit, and on-chain execution linkage.
